title: Conditional insertion of the Q3 weighted mixed rate into a first-passage Poisson bridge
question: If the exact-Q3 response has a factorial first-passage expansion, what spatial decay exponent follows when the EXP-001045 weighted mixed local rate, six-neighbour degree, and two orientations are inserted?
method: Recompute B from the EXP-001045 onsite, edge and bond exact rate fixture.
Multiply B by the declared orientation count, six-neighbour path count, spatial tilt base and time to obtain the exact exponent E.
Apply the distance factor base^(-d) and compare the finite order-32 Poisson partial sum with exp(E) in two exact lanes.
Compile Lean R228 for B, E, the distance factor and the finite arithmetic fixture.
Keep the factorial first-passage expansion explicitly as an unresolved hypothesis.
finding: Under the declared factorial first-passage hypothesis, the EXP-001045 rate B=1382807/7168 gives E=4148421/896000 for two orientations, degree six, base two, and t=1/1000. At distance ten the conditional envelope is 2^(-10) exp(E), and the finite order-32 partial sum is below exp(E).
decision_reason: This is a parameterized insertion of an actual Q3 weighted mixed rate into the existing first-passage bridge. It does not discharge the factorial response hypothesis, so the main Q3 history/common-alpha gate remains open.

adversarial_review.check: B is recomputed from EXP-001045 rather than pasted.
The factor two is explicit and separate from degree six.
The six-neighbour path count is conditional graph combinatorics.
Finite partial sums do not prove an infinite operator history.
No thermodynamic QFT, KMS/OS, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A result follows.
